summary: The cluster-scale receipt (4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a) scored cleanly: with RestoreCommittedLogs all three voters come back empty and no leader emerges (violated, witness index 1), while the same simultaneous restart without the flag keeps all three configured and re-elects (control holds, index 3). The interpretation now cites four receipts including that one, confirming a cluster-wide rather than single-node loss. I also ran a partial-restart probe: with only two of three voters restarted, the untouched configured voter leads with the configuration-less nodes' votes (servers [0,0,3]), and once that voter stops, the two remaining live, fully up-to-date voters (log index 13 on both) cannot elect a leader in six seconds at 50ms timeouts — while the no-flag control re-elects immediately. That experiment is submitted for a retained receipt, and I registered a new gap asking whether the silently produced two-server change ({A,B,C} -> {A,B,E}) can let running nodes hold disjoint majorities and elect two leaders.
